Lilim House

A new house above a green valley, made calm and finished from the first night.

Location
Antipolo, Rizal
Type
Residential, family house
Floor area
320 sqm
Service
Full-Service Furnishing
Year
2025
Duration
18 weeks from signed proposal to handover, with 6 days on site

The brief

A family of five moved into the first house they built, on a hillside above a green valley. The contractor handed it over white, tiled, and empty. They wanted it calm and finished from the first night, with the view left open and nothing more built.

As handed over

A new house, finished by the contractor and empty. White painted walls, pale gray tile, flat white ceilings with recessed downlights, bronze aluminum sliding doors, and a bare bulb at each ceiling point.

The approach

The house looks over a valley, and green fills every opening. We kept the great room quiet, so the valley is the color. Charcoal linen, black wood, and steel sit against white linen, pale wool, and gray Romblon marble. One stone table, made for the house, leads the living room. Cane and warm wood appear in every room.

The builder left cool ceiling lights. We changed every bulb to a warm one and added lamps where the family sits, eats, and reads. White linen runs from the ceiling for the full length of the glass. We left the middle of the great room open, because three children need a floor. Their books, their games, and the screen have a room of their own. Nothing was built or painted.

The moves

  1. 1

    Linen from the ceiling, for the whole length of the glass.

    Fifteen meters of white linen on ceiling tracks. The bronze frames soften and the room grows taller.

  2. 2

    One slab of stone at the center.

    The seating gathers around it.

  3. 3

    Dark against pale, with warm wood and cane.

    Charcoal, black wood, and steel against white linen, pale wool, and gray stone. The valley is the green.

  4. 4

    Every bulb changed, and lamps where people sit.

    The cool ceiling lights became warm and dimmable. Lamps do the rest.

  5. 5

    The family’s own things, framed and placed.

    The children’s drawings are framed and hung in the family room. The grandmother’s jar stands by the sofa. Three hundred books fill one wall.

Living

The Silong Sofa in charcoal linen faces a daybed made for the house, across one slab of Romblon marble. The first view, seen from the entry in late afternoon, is the pair at the top of the page.

Dining

At dusk the Kapis Pendant lights the ebonized Hapag Dining Table and six Hain Dining Chairs.

Kitchen

The builder’s kitchen, with stools made for the counter and a Lenta Pendant above it. Breakfast happens here.

Family room

The Yakap Sofa faces a wall of the family’s books, with the screen on a Baul Credenza.

Entry

Shoes come off here, and keys go in the tray.

Main bedroom

The ebonized Himlay Bed in morning light, under a woven panel made for the room by Tikog Loom.

Children’s room

Two beds made for the house, the Aparador Cabinet, and a wall for the children’s own drawings.

Terrace and exterior

The Duyan Daybed and the Batis Coffee Table face the valley in the early sun. At dusk, every room is lit.

Materials
